turns.user: Why are there so many more holdings than Strategy 1?

replies.content:
Strategy 2 holds **13 assets** and Strategy 1 holds **4**. The difference comes from how each one spreads your money.

- **Strategy 1** puts about 30% each into GLD, XOM, GOOGL and RY.TO. It is concentrated, so a fall in a few holdings has a larger effect on the whole portfolio.
- **Strategy 2** spreads money across broad ETFs (VTI, QQQ, XIU.TO), Canadian REITs, bonds (AGG, 7.3%) and individual stocks. Its largest holding is 29.6%.

Here is how the two compare in the backtest (April 2026 to November 2026):

| | Strategy 1 | Strategy 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Assets held | 4 | 13 |
| Backtest volatility | 12.8% | 12.1% |
| Max drawdown | -9.2% | -4.5% |
| Total return | 0.4% | 10.8% |

Strategy 2 had a smaller maximum drawdown and higher volatility was lower, but this is one short test period, so it doesn't show how either will perform in the future.
